facts.d: The whipper-in was the rider who kept stray hounds with the pack. Edmund Burke first applied the term to Parliament, and it stuck — a piece of eighteenth-century hunting slang now embedded in Indian constitutional practice.

facts.t: Breaking a three-line whip in Britain costs you the party, not the seat
facts.d: A rebel MP loses the party whip and sits as an independent, keeping the constituency. In India the same act can end the career outright, because the Tenth Schedule attaches disqualification to the vote.

facts.t: The whip has no mention in the Constitution
facts.d: Neither the office nor the instrument appears anywhere in the constitutional text or in any statute. It is a party convention that the Tenth Schedule made legally consequential without ever defining.

bank.q: Who first used the term whip in a political sense?
bank.e: Edmund Burke, borrowing from the foxhunting whipper-in who kept hounds with the pack.

bank.q: With reference to whips in India, consider the following statements:
s: The anti-defection law gives legal force to whip compliance.
The Minister and Minister of State for Parliamentary Affairs serve as Government Chief Whips.
Opposition parties do not appoint whips.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Opposition parties appoint their own whips as well.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT among the roles of a whip?
o: Certifying a Bill as a Money Bill
Acting as a communication link between leadership and members
bank.e: Money Bill certification is the Speaker's function under Article 110, not the whip's.

bank.q: Match List I (country) with List II (whip practice):
pairs: 2. Breaking a three-line whip makes an MP independent, not disqualified
bank.e: Britain's political-only consequence, America's informal whips, Australia's recognised conscience votes, and India's legally enforced compliance.

bank.as: The whip system is criticised as undemocratic.
bank.rs: It restricts a legislator's freedom to vote according to conscience or constituency interest.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion. The proposed remedy is to codify the scope of whips rather than to abolish them.

bank.q: Consider the following reform proposals on whips:
s: The 170th Law Commission recommended codifying the scope of whips.
The NCRWC recommended differentiating between categories of legislative issues.
The Second ARC recommended abolishing whips entirely.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Second ARC's recommendation concerned internal party democracy, not abolition.

bank.q: All of the following are identified as problems with the whip system EXCEPT:
o: Lack of transparency in issuing whips
Excessive judicial interference in party discipline
bank.e: Courts stay out of internal party discipline. The problems identified are internal to the party and parliamentary system.

bank.q: Which former Vice-President is associated with the call to revise the anti-defection law in relation to whips?
bank.e: Hamid Ansari, who as Rajya Sabha Chairman repeatedly argued for confining whips to matters affecting the government's survival.

bank.q: With reference to enforcement, consider the following statements:
s: Violating a three-line whip can lead to disqualification or expulsion in India.
Whips serve an early-warning function by monitoring discontent.
The whip is a statutory office defined under the Representation of the People Act.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The whip has no statutory basis at all — it is a party convention given consequence by the Tenth Schedule.

bank.q: Which of the following best captures the proposed reimagining of the whip?
o: A symbol of control rather than coordination
A tool of coordination and an enabler of responsible freedom
An instrument to be abolished in favour of free votes on all matters
A statutory office with judicial oversight
bank.e: Coordination rather than control — discipline aligned with dialogue, in the formulation used to close the discussion.
